title: What if every Starlink satellite fell at once?
premise: All of the more than 10,000 Starlink satellites drop out of orbit on the same night.

intro.title: What if every *Starlink* satellite fell at once?
intro.subtitle: A HYPOTHETICAL SCENARIO

beats.caption: SpaceX now has more than ten thousand satellites circling Earth.

tooltip.label: FACT
tooltip.text: They fly about 550 km up, moving at roughly 27,000 km/h.

beats.caption: Each one circles the planet in about an hour and a half.
Then, one night, they all start falling.
Thousands of fireballs streak across the sky at once.

tooltip.label: BY DESIGN
tooltip.text: Starlink satellites are built to burn up completely on re-entry.

beats.caption: Almost none would ever reach the ground.
Ships in the middle of the ocean suddenly lose their internet.
So do millions of homes, planes and remote towns.

tooltip.label: OPEN QUESTION
tooltip.text: Scientists are studying whether metal ash from burned-up satellites could affect the ozone layer.

beats.caption: Tons of metal ash would linger high in the atmosphere.
Replacing them all would take years of launches.
